info.name: ELK Backend
info.description:
Every route the NestJS controllers actually declare — generated from them, so it cannot drift into listing endpoints that do not exist.

Global prefix `api` with URI versioning `v1`, so paths are `/api/v1/...`. The two exceptions are `/health/live` and `/health/ready`, which are excluded from the prefix.

**Start here:** Auth > "Send a one-time passcode", then "Verify a phone OTP". The verify request saves `accessToken` and `refreshToken` into the environment, and every other request reads the token from there.

Responses are wrapped: the payload is under `data`.

Bodies show the *required* fields with sample values; optional ones are left out. Query parameters are listed with the optional ones disabled.
